description: Mechanical cross-check of central_bridge_triangle_final.md Part X.0: exhaustively over all 4 rows of central_bridge_triangle.md Part V.1's (X_x,X_y) table, the two admissible-pair terminal sets {x,X_x} and {y,X_y} always either coincide or share exactly one element -- a genuinely 4-distinct-terminal 'crossing' configuration never occurs, since both sets are 2-subsets of the single 3-element triangle T. This is the exact resolution of the task's flagged-incomplete X.3 crossing case: it does not occur in this triangle-anchored setting.
scope_note: This is a complete enumeration over the only 4 possible (X_x,X_y) configurations (X_x in T\{x}, 2 choices; X_y in T\{y}, 2 choices), not a sampled search -- matching exactly central_bridge_triangle.md Part V.1's table. Does not address the separate, still-open general crossing case for arbitrary witness-path pairs elsewhere in G (contraction_intersections.md Part V.3), which this file explicitly does not claim to resolve.
note_on_python_version: Matches the repository's .python-version pin; this check is pure combinatorics and does not import NetworkX.
detector_agreement: Direct exhaustive enumeration in Python, independent of the hand-derived pigeonhole argument (two 2-subsets of a 3-set always coincide or share exactly one element). The row order is now explicit and its stdout hash was reproduced under PYTHONHASHSEED=1,2,3,99. 0 disagreements.
completed_range: Complete enumeration of all 4 possible (X_x,X_y) configurations -- exhaustive, not sampled, consistent with the phase's explicit decision not to launch broad computation.
